title: Cooling System Diagnostics
summary: Compact cooling-system hub for overheating, coolant loss, thermostat, water pump, radiator fan, and pressure-test workflows.
intro: Use this hub when temperature behavior, coolant loss, fan operation, heater output, or steam/smell complaints need to be sorted before pricing cooling parts.

diagnostic_path_sections.title: Leak and Pressure Path
diagnostic_path_sections.summary: Start here when coolant level drops, smell is present, or residue is visible.
checks: Pressure test the system cold and inspect cap, hoses, radiator, pump, and heater connections
Confirm coolant type and contamination before topping off
Check for internal leak signs when external leaks are not found
confidence_cues: External and internal leaks can overlap

diagnostic_path_sections.title: Airflow and Fan Path
diagnostic_path_sections.summary: Use when temperature rises at idle, in traffic, or with AC load.
checks: Command or observe fan operation with AC on and coolant temperature rising
Inspect fan fuses, relays, connectors, shroud, and condenser/radiator airflow
Compare overheating at idle versus highway speed
confidence_cues: AC load is a useful fan test clue
Airflow checks come before coolant parts

diagnostic_path_sections.title: Thermostat and Circulation Path
diagnostic_path_sections.summary: Use when warm-up, heater output, P0128, or hose temperature patterns are the main clue.
checks: Compare scan-tool coolant temperature to hose temperature behavior
Inspect for trapped air after prior cooling work
Check heater output and circulation evidence before replacing the thermostat
confidence_cues: P0128 does not prove only one part

inspection_priority: Verify coolant level, leak evidence, and pressure-test results first.
Compare overheating at idle, with AC on, and at road speed.
Confirm fan operation, thermostat behavior, and air bleeding before replacing parts.
confidence_cues: Fan and airflow checks matter at idle
Bleeding and coolant condition affect final approval
estimate_guidance: Include coolant bleeding/refill considerations with thermostat, pump, radiator, or fan-related estimates.
Separate external leak repair from internal coolant-intrusion concerns.
Add diagnostic time when overheating behavior changes with AC load or vehicle speed.
